title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: parent-level permissions for ServiceNow and Confluence
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, connector permission behaviour, licensing requirements and admin paths are supported. It correctly reports Microsoft's conflicting Confluence documentation rather than choosing one version. The governance checklist still names service-account and identity controls that are missing from its controls table.

claims.quote: Admins can manage access more precisely with support for nested permissions in Jira, Confluence, and ServiceNow; Support for hierarchical ACLs for SNOW, Confluence, Jira connectors.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Simple is the default ServiceNow Knowledge user-criteria flow.
claims.quote: The ServiceNow Knowledge connector supports two flows for user criteria permissions: Simple (default) and Advanced. Both flows evaluate knowledge base (parent)-level and article (child)-level user criteria.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Simple flow does not evaluate advanced script-based user criteria.
claims.quote: The default is Simple. In this flow, advanced script-based user criteria aren't evaluated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: On the Can Read path, Simple skips advanced script-based criteria and might overshare.
claims.quote: If an advanced script-based user criterion exists on the Can Read (allow) path of a knowledge base or article, the Simple flow can't evaluate the script to determine which users are allowed, so it skips that user criterion, which might result in oversharing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: On the Cannot Read path, Simple treats advanced script-based criteria as deny all and blocks the affected content for all users.
claims.quote: To avoid oversharing restricted content, the connector conservatively treats the criterion as deny all, so the affected knowledge base or article content is blocked for all users in Copilot and search results.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Advanced flow is the documented alternative that evaluates ServiceNow Knowledge advanced script-based user criteria.
claims.quote: To evaluate advanced script-based user criteria correctly, use the Advanced flow and Set up REST API.

claims.claim: Advanced flow requires a Scripted REST API set up in ServiceNow.
claims.quote: This flow evaluates script-based user criteria by calling the Scripted REST API in ServiceNow, which ensures accurate permissions handling when content is ingested into Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: If the ServiceNow service account cannot read sys_properties, permission evaluation defaults to the most restrictive settings.
claims.quote: If the service account can't read these properties, the connector silently defaults to the most restrictive settings (true for both), which blocks articles without explicit user criteria from appearing in search results.

claims.claim: Those restrictive fallback settings can prevent articles without explicit user criteria from appearing in results.
claims.quote: If the service account can't read these properties, the connector defaults to the most restrictive settings, which can cause articles without explicit user criteria to not appear in search results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: For HR Service Delivery knowledge bases in the sn_hr_core scope, the service account needs sn_hr_core.content_reader or sn_hr_core.admin.
claims.quote: If your ServiceNow instance uses the HR Service Delivery module with knowledge bases in the Human Resources: Core (sn_hr_core) application scope, assign one of the following roles to the service account. sn_hr_core.content_reader; sn_hr_core.admin

claims.claim: Without one of those HR roles, HR-restricted articles might be indexed as accessible to all users.
claims.quote: Because the connector receives empty results rather than an error, it might interpret HR-restricted articles as having no access restrictions and index them as accessible to all users.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Visible to everyone grants all organisation users access regardless of source ACLs.
claims.quote: You can choose not to enforce per-user permissions (setting the connector to index content as Visible to everyone). In that case, all indexed Confluence data is searchable by any user in the tenant.

claims.claim: Only people with access to this data source makes the connector respect source ACLs.
claims.quote: Only people with access to this data source: The connector respects source system access control lists (ACLs).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Confluence overview says email-to-UPN mismatches require manual mapping.
claims.quote: If your Confluence users' email IDs do not exactly match their Entra ID user principal names (UPNs), an admin must configure a manual identity mapping so the system knows which Microsoft 365 user corresponds to each Confluence account.

claims.claim: The Confluence overview says missing identity mapping can hide content from intended users.
claims.quote: Without this mapping, some content might not appear for intended users because the service can't verify that they have access.

claims.claim: The Confluence setup page describes default matching against either Entra ID UPN or email address.
claims.quote: The default method for mapping your data source identities to Microsoft Entra ID is to determine whether the email address of each Confluence user matches the user principal name (UPN) or email address in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: ServiceNow standard incremental crawls do not update article permissions when knowledge-base parent permissions change.
claims.quote: Incremental crawl - Syncs changed content and recomputes permissions for those changed articles and article-level permission changes. Doesn't update user-to-criteria mappings (identity sync) or permissions for articles where knowledge base (parent) level permissions changed.

claims.claim: The default Confluence full-crawl interval is 24 hours.
claims.quote: Permission changes are picked up only during a full crawl (once every 24 hours by default), not during the 15-minute incremental syncs.

claims.quote: By syncing LDAP groups into Confluence, administrators can assign those groups to spaces and pages to control view and edit access to align with enterprise-wide identity governance.

claims.claim: Confluence page restrictions are configured in Confluence.
claims.quote: If a page has specific view restrictions, the page is only visible to authorized users in responses and search results. If no page-level restriction exists, the connector applies the Confluence space permissions settings.
